evidence.summary: 为 DSH Web 提供 Host 权威任务看板，绑定真实会话执行、Cron 调度和可选 goal 验收。
limitations: 功能摘要根据作者固定版本材料归纳，不是逐字引文或独立效果验证。

evidence.summary: 核查 packages/dsh-task-board/package.json、packages/dsh-task-board/src/core/handover.ts、packages/dsh-task-board/src/core/spend-budget.ts、packages/dsh-task-board/src/core/use-cases/task-update.ts、packages/dsh-task-board/src/core/verification.ts、packages/dsh-task-board/src/host-ledger.ts、packages/dsh-task-board/src/host-routes.ts、packages/dsh-task-board/src/host-runner.ts、packages/dsh-task-board/src/host-service.ts、packages/dsh-task-board/src/host/agent-tools.ts、packages/dsh-task-board/src/host/llm-dispatch.ts、packages/dsh-task-board/src/host/verification-gate.ts、packages/dsh-task-board/src/host/verification-runner.ts、packages/dsh-task-board/src/index.ts；Host action→ledger execution先提交→runner真实create/reuse/prompt→轮询history结算；可选enforced goal完成前模型验收门禁，cron由Host arm未来时刻，见 [Q02](#research-q02)至 [Q05](#research-q05)。
limitations: 子包package/index注册；action→ledger run/requestcache/permission/commit；runner workspace/preset/create/reuse/pin/prompt/goal/inspect；HTTP多分支trust；verification gate/runner/prepared dispatch/pass算法；cron/不可读轮询/卸载和manual settle。未执行/全Web UI/所有import/extension/子树继承与dispatcher/team/GitHub/attachment/上游Host权限/锁迁移/真实调度和裁判准确率。

findings.text: 能审查巡检/编码结果的DSH维护者，用临时workspace单卡核执行与来源，再决定开调度/验收，见 [Q01](#research-q01)。
Host action→ledger execution先提交→runner真实create/reuse/prompt→轮询history结算；可选enforced goal完成前模型验收门禁，cron由Host arm未来时刻，见 [Q02](#research-q02)至 [Q05](#research-q05)。

子包package/index注册；action→ledger run/requestcache/permission/commit；runner workspace/preset/create/reuse/pin/prompt/goal/inspect；HTTP多分支trust；verification gate/runner/prepared dispatch/pass算法；cron/不可读轮询/卸载和manual settle。未执行/全Web UI/所有import/extension/子树继承与dispatcher/team/GitHub/attachment/上游Host权限/锁迁移/真实调度和裁判准确率。
同仓原生Host/Web任务执行子包；目录集合不代表远程/插件管理/团队等其他包已验。

#### 成本

| 阶段 | 现金/资源 | 人工 | 边界 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 首次 | Host/模型/可写ledger | 绑定workspace/权限/准则 | 未测时长 |
| 持续 | 执行/goal/多轮judge/存储 | 查来源/裁判误判/插件兼容 | token cap非现金硬cap |
| 失败 | 已飞模型与外部影响 | 查真实目标/unknown/写盘 | 账本cancelled非停止 |
| 退出 | 卡片/会话/产物保留 | 停规则和真实工作/清理 | 卸载不撤副作用 |
临时workspace单张只读卡先关自动面跑一次，再独立核goal裁判；任何观测失败/状态未知先查真实session和目标再处理，不自动rerun，见 [Q06](#research-q06)。

#### 效果

| 项目 | 当前支持 | 未确认 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 委派 | ledger→真实session/prompt | 实际任务成功率 |
| 验收 | enforced completion必须pass | 模型判分事实准确 |
| 调度 | Host cron未来arm/skip | 离线/休眠及时执行 |
| 来源 | 手工/外部/普通/enforced可区分 | 用户是否误信失败重跑 |
| 成本控制 | 已测日token拒新run | cash/在飞强停/净省时 |
execution预绑定/请求fingerprint、冻结验收合约、多类异常和真实ledger fsync明确；范围是Host状态流程非跨目标事务，取消/观察失败/内存持久需精确解释，见 [Q02](#research-q02)至 [Q05](#research-q05)。
将任务委派、Host持久execution/session与可选completion程序验收连起来，关闭浏览器不依赖前端tick，用户可回查来源而非只看列，见 [Q02](#research-q02)/[Q04](#research-q04)。
确认stamp和本机访问非可信人批/租户保证；普通turn/手工Done与enforced不同，裁判pass非事实真相；手工settle仅关账本、历史不可读failed也可能目标已完成，见 [Q03](#research-q03)至 [Q05](#research-q05)。
为连续历史不可读的观测失败提供需核目标的unknown呈现，对照现有已说明未知的error文字，误重跑不降或增加悬挂负担即否定，见 [Q07](#research-q07)。

#### 依赖

| 条件 | 用途 | 缺失/边界 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DSH>=0.2.2-rc.1/React成品 | 原生Host/Web | 声明不等运行验收 |
| gateway/workspace/preset/commands | 会话/pin/goal | 无workspace不落Host cwd |
| Host权限与本机可信路由 | 动作/提权流程 | cookie有fallback分支，非租户隔离 |
| 模型/可选judge与goal | 真实执行/验收 | 配置冻结，goal不可用可普通turn |
| 可写ledger/会话日志 | 结果历史 | 不等外部效果共同事务 |
| 持续Host/平台电源能力 | cron/可选idle保护 | missed不补跑/不能唤醒 |

technical.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)看板/cron/模型judge成熟，DSH execution/goal结合有局部组合故novelty25%超0，未证新范式不达50%。[Q02](#research-q02)/[Q04](#research-q04)冻结contract、实际pre-execute gate与异常预算改变完成声明准入，mechanism50%超25%只列UI；裁判/绑定/全部恢复未验不达75%。[Q05](#research-q05)ledger/观察失败与外部影响分层可迁移，transferability50%超25%局部样式，缺跨Host验证不达75%。simplification25%，[Q06](#research-q06)集中委派/历史少手工串联超0，维护模型/权限/unknown仍重不达50%。

business.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)/[Q05](#research-q05)用户从直接逐轮发prompt改为持久卡委派给Host/cron，Host启动/结算、用户审结果和返工，任务组织和交接真实改变，workflow25%超0便利；多角色团队/稳定生产效果未证不达50%。delivery25%，[Q04](#research-q04)enforced执行交付需带本次acceptance pass/问题反馈，区别只给聊天完成声明，超0；模型不等独立业务验收、普通/手工仍可绕范围，不达50%。reach0无此前受限明确群体接入，不因Agent自然语言工具升25%。economics0，[Q06](#research-q06)模型/判分多耗、token日闸不改资源供给/服务结构，集中看板和省手工不当25%。

recommendation.reason: 能审查任务结果的 DSH 维护者，可在临时工作区用一张只读卡试真实会话执行。它把委派、Host 台账、会话与可选验收记录连在一起，便于回查每次运行。遇到历史不可读、账本取消或目标结果不明时，应停止自动重跑并先核实际会话与产物。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01)/[Q06](#research-q06)维护任务委派/原会话基线与单卡结果明确，50%超25%泛管理；真实长期需求与生产成功率未验不达75%。

advantage.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)/[Q04](#research-q04)真实execution与可选门禁超25%普通列，50%；裁判误判/unknown/全程成本无对照不达75%。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02)真create/prompt/inspect、[Q04](#research-q04)真judge请求/判定与[Q05](#research-q05)持久/退出已查，50%超25%声明；运行/全部UI权限/调度及故障无实测不达75%。

cost.rationale: [Q03](#research-q03)-[Q06](#research-q06)权限/模型judge/Host在线/状态unknown维护显著，25%不达50%轻负担；单只读卡关自动面与手工退路超0。

publication.summaries.text: 为 DSH Web 提供 Host 权威任务看板，绑定真实会话执行、Cron 调度和可选 goal 验收。

items.界面: 任务卡片与执行/验收历史视图
items.模型工具: Agent可建改/运行/调度任务卡
items.Host 路由: 本机/受信代理action API与状态

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 用途 | 条件与边界 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 卡片/手工列 | 组织声明 | Done可无Host执行 |
| 会话执行 | workspace/preset/权限绑定 | prompt入队非完成 |
| goal验收 | enforce完成门禁 | opt-in/模型判断非事实证明 |
| cron | Host未来触发 | missed不补跑/Host在线 |
| 提权闸 | resolved binding+stamp | GUI流程非可信签名 |
| 预算/电源 | 拒新run/可选idle保护 | token非money/非唤醒 |

publication.advice.text: 临时workspace单张只读卡先关自动面跑一次，再独立核goal裁判；任何观测失败/状态未知先查真实session和目标再处理，不自动rerun，见 [Q06](#research-q06)。

      "content": "# dsh-task-board · Autonomous Task Board & Cron Scheduling for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)\n\nEnglish | [中文](README.zh.md)\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@linxin666/dsh-task-board?style=flat-square\" alt=\"Version\">\n   \n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%3E%3D0.2.2--rc.1-4c6ef5?style=flat-square&labelColor=454a54\" alt=\"DSH\">\n   \n  <img src=\"https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue?style=flat-square\" alt=\"License\">\n</p>\n\n<p align=\"center\">\n  <strong>Autonomous Kanban Task Board & Cron Scheduling for DeepSeek Harness (DSH)</strong><br>\n  <em>Host-Authoritative Ledger · Parent-Card Subtask Dispatch · Double-Blind Verification · Sleep Inhibition · GitHub Issue-to-PR</em>\n</p>\n\nA hot-pluggable DeepSeek Harness (DSH) Web GUI and official desktop client task automation plugin with a Host-authoritative task ledger, real DSH agent session execution, cron background scheduling, cross-platform idle-sleep protection, parent-card subtask dispatch, and automated verification quality gates. It executes unattended background workflows including automated code reviews, routine health checks, and scheduled pipelines without requiring an open browser window. It mounts cleanly via `cordis.patch.yml` and profiles without modifying DSH core code.\n\n- Host-authoritative architecture and offline background execution: The browser is merely an asynchronous view; closing tabs or dropping connections will not interrupt Host scheduling, session execution, or atomic ledger settlement. Built-in cross-platform sleep inhibition (macOS, Windows, Linux) allows screens to power down while preventing system idle sleep for reliable unattended automation.\n- Parent-card dispatch over subtask trees: a task can carry subtasks, one to three levels deep as the deployment allows. Running a card opens one session, that card's own: the Host opens nothing for its subtasks, and that session reads them with `task_board_get`, dispatches them with `subagent` in dependency order, and writes their conclusions back with `task_board_manage` before it finishes. A card whose subtasks are still unfinished runs under the liangshen dispatcher preset.\n- Double-blind adversarial judge quality gates (No False Completion): Intercepts false agent completion claims; requires verification by an independent Judge Model using strict coding criteria, a 0.65 threshold, two-round A/B position swapping, and validation against real workspace filesystem diffs, returning actionable diagnostics for self-repair.\n- Automated GitHub loop, freeze handover, and agent tool surface: Real-time bidirectional GitHub Issues sync automates agent bug fixing and PR creation; supports `<<<FREEZE` session context snapshots with handover packages; exposes 8 native model tools for autonomous planning and external execution registration.\n\n## Features\n\nCards keep multi-line title and description previews with visible metadata. Previews strip Markdown formatting; task details render description and prompt as safe Markdown without raw HTML or automatic remote images, and content taller than about eight rendered lines is clamped to a fixed height with a fade hint and a \"Show more\" toggle that expands and collapses it, while shorter content renders untouched with no toggle. Stored task text is unchanged. A bracketed title prefix such as `[Bug]:` renders as a type badge, and the description preview skips issue-form boilerplate (checkbox lists, section headings, empty-field placeholders), preferring a summary section when one exists. A left stripe shows the latest run (running, succeeded, failed, cancelled); a card whose column disagrees with that run is labelled as set by hand. Each column shows the time its cards differ by — created in Backlog/To Do, started while running, settled in Done/Failed — read in the Host time zone. The latest execution session opens straight from the card. Every column header toggles compact single-line cards (Done starts compact, the choice is stored in the browser). All five columns and the archive first group cards by provider source — full `owner/repository` labels for GitHub — with unclaimed cards in Local tasks; source groups sort by label and their fold choices persist per browser. Done source groups start collapsed while the other columns and the archive start expanded, and search always reveals matching groups. Done, Failed and the archive nest Today / Last 7 days / Earlier within each source group and fold the oldest group once that source holds more than 30 cards, unless a search is active.\n\n- **Task board UI**: the board is the shell's own center-column panel — like the desktop application's Plugins page, it contributes a row to the shell's official sidebar panel list and a page to the layout's center-column seat, so row geometry, the active highlight, the collapsed rail, the label, and language switching are the shell's to own; the board provides five kanban columns, search, task details, archive/restore, execution history, and links to execution transcripts. Every column is reachable by hand, by dragging a card or from the detail view's move menu: the move writes the column and no execution record, so Done or Failed declares work that finished (or failed) outside a tracked run and Running parks work that is under way without a session, while a card the runner is actually executing refuses every move until it settles. Archived tasks are read-only except for restore, delete, and transcript viewing, and cannot run manually or on schedule until restored.\n- **Two complementary automation entries**: the shell's official *Automation tasks* page manages reminders and timed prompts in the Host Schedule service, while *Task board* manages cards, subtasks, real Session execution, cron, acceptance, and execution history. Both entries stay available so the user can choose the task shape; the board neither hides nor takes over the official page.\n- **Detail layout and folds**: the task detail is two columns on a wide viewport — the left holds the task itself (description, execution prompt, labels, subtasks, frozen snapshot, handover bundle) and the right holds how this run will run (execution settings, scheduled runs, execution history, status); a narrow viewport falls back to one column in the same order. Workspace, agent preset, permission, model, and reasoning effort stay visible, while the three card-level switches (continue in the same conversation, start with /goal, skip this task's acceptance) fold into one \"Advanced\" row that echoes the switches that are on while it is closed, so the card's shape is readable without expanding it. Scheduled runs and execution history each take one fold row: the schedule row says whether a rule is armed and when it next fires, the history row says how many runs there are and what the latest one did, and the list itself shows the five most recent runs until it is expanded; an acceptance report shows one verdict badge on its row and the verdict, judge route, per-criterion scores, and findings only once expanded. The permission gate and the current status never fold. The view uses three type sizes (title, body, meta), status and result badges share one filled slot scale, and every fold row and button carries a hit target of at least 44 pixels.\n- **Continuation cards (data plane)**: a new task may paste a `<<<FREEZE ... >>>FREEZE` block from a session; it parses into a goal/progress/next snapshot persisted with the task (ledger v3). Cards carry a frozen badge, the detail view shows the full snapshot and freeze time, search covers snapshot text, and archive/restore matches plain tasks. The snapshot reuses the freeze security gate at the protocol layer: sensitive patterns become `[REDACTED]` with a marker, slash-prefixed command lines reject the whole snapshot, and each field is capped at 8 KiB.\n- **Handover bundles and the permission confirmation gate**: a continuation card may attach a handover bundle — the pinned execution triplet (workspace / agent preset / permission) plus doc/script references. The bundle's triplet overrides the plain pin fields at execution, and the references ride the prompt as a handover preamble. A binding whose effective permission is above the deployment's permission baseline — the Host's own default permission preset unless the profile pins `sessionDefaultPermission` — is unconfirmed: manual run refuses, cron skips the card and rolls to the next occurrence, and the confirm button in the task detail resolves the binding; any later permission or bundle change re-arms the gate.\n- **Claim provenance wrap and source audit**: executing a continuation card (a card with a frozen snapshot) mandatorily wraps the task instruction in a source-declaration template — freeze instant, source session, and an unreviewed-content warning — composed after the handover preamble so the picking-up agent stays wary of stored prompt injection in card text. The session issuing a create/update action is stamped into the snapshot (frozenBy, re-stamped when the snapshot is replaced), and the session issuing a run/rerun lands on the execution record (initiatedBy) together with a captured copy of the freeze provenance; both are visible in the task detail. The initiator is client-asserted audit metadata, not a trust boundary.\n- **Task tags (issue #1521)**: a task may carry up to eight labels. A label renders as a colour-toned badge on the card — the tone is hashed from the name, so one label always paints the same way and no colour is stored — the board header gains a multi-select tag filter built from every label in use (including archived tasks), and search also matches label names. A label with an \"execution hint\" is injected ahead of the execution prompt on every run as a `标签提示` block; a label without one is display and filter only, so an untagged task's prompt is byte-for-byte what it was before the feature. Labels stay editable after the first run: they classify the task and shape the next run, they are not the record of what already ran. A **Manage labels** action on the filter row opens the label manager: every label in use with the number of tasks carrying it, a rename that rewrites the label on every card (merging into an existing label of that name and keeping that label's execution hint), and a delete that removes it from every task including archived ones. Both are ledger-wide Host transactions, so several windows looking at one board stay consistent.\n- **Label cleanup**: a **Cleanup** row in the label manager takes a threshold (5 by default, 1 to 99) and removes the labels the board has stopped using. A label is a candidate when fewer than that many tasks carry it and every one of those tasks is already done or failed; archived cards count on the same terms, so an archived card that settled lets its label go while a card that is archived and still unfinished keeps it. Cleanup works out its candidates before it writes anything: with none it only says so and leaves the ledger alone, and with some it opens the confirm dialog listing each label with its task count, after which each of them goes through the same ledger-wide delete the manager's own delete button uses. The label leaves every card including archived ones, its execution hint goes with it, and no task is otherwise touched; the removal cannot be undone.\n- **Subtasks and parent-card dispatch**: a task can be given subtasks, either by creating one from its detail view (the form starts from the parent's workspace, preset, permission, and model, and each stays overridable) or by linking an existing task that has no parent yet; a subtask can be detached again once it is not running. The lineage gate lives in the Host: the parent must exist and be on board, a task can never be attached under one of its own descendants, and a tree may not exceed the configured `maxSubtaskDepth` (1 by default, 3 maximum). Running a card opens one session for that card and none for its subtasks, and running a subtask directly is the same operation: that card is the root of the run even when it carries a parent and subtasks of its own, and nothing under it is expanded. A subtask already in the done column is outside the run's dispatch set, so finishing subtasks one by one and then running the parent costs one session instead of a repeat of the tree; move it back to the todo column to have it dispatched again. The board marks parent and subtask cards, the detail view lists the direct subtasks and says what one run will do, and the header offers a one-click hide-subtasks filter.\n- **Parent-card dispatch and subtask accounting**: clicking a card that carries unfinished subtasks opens that card's own session and nothing else. The run is forced under the `liangshen` dispatcher preset shipped by `packages/dsh-liangshen`, the card's stored agent preset is never rewritten, and session reuse is skipped so the run mints a fresh session; a deployment that registers no `liangshen` preset fails the run closed, with that missing preset as the reason on the card. The prompt names every unfinished subtask with its title, task id, and status, states that no session is opened for them, and asks the session to read each card with `task_board_get`, dispatch it with `subagent` in dependency order (independent ones may run together), and write each conclusion back with `task_board_manage({action:'record-external-outcome'})` before it finishes. A conclusion the session never wrote back is supplied by the Host when the card's own run ends: every still-unrecorded unfinished subtask inherits that verdict as an external record whose initiator reads `parent-run:<card id>` and whose reason says the card ran no session of its own and inherited the parent run's conclusion. The backfill is idempotent, and a cancelled parent writes nothing. A card with no unfinished subtask is unaffected.\n- **Project partition (issue #1536)**: the board header offers a project row built from the deployment's DSH workspaces — \"all projects\" plus one entry per registered project. Selecting a project narrows the columns to the tasks pinned to it, and tasks with no pinned workspace stay visible under \"all projects\". Opening the new-task form while a project is open preselects that project as the task's workspace, and \"new project…\" registers a host directory through the same runtime call the GUI's own add-project uses. A root task created without a project choice — from the form or through the board's agent tool — inherits the workspace of the session that created it, and a card that still pins nothing runs in the deployment's most recently used workspace instead of the Host's own working directory.\n- **AI parse of pasted text (issue #1540)**: the new-task form takes text copied from anywhere and has a model turn it into the title, description, and run prompt. The model is one of the deployment's configured models (the same list the task's model pin uses, first entry preselected), and the call runs on the Host behind the board's usual loopback and same-origin fence, with a 45 s budget and a cancel affordance. The draft only fills the form: nothing is created until the task is submitted, and a failed parse leaves what you already typed untouched.\n- **Collapsible task form**: the create/duplicate/subtask dialog groups its configuration into collapsible regions — task content open by default, then labels, execution settings, run mode, handover, and scheduled runs — and every collapsed region keeps a one-line summary of the values it holds, so the dialog fits without a scrollbar (its body keeps an overflow fallback for very short windows). The agent-preset field is named \"Agent preset\" and lists the deployment's built-in presets under localized names plus any user preset, with an inherit default that names the preset a run without a pin actually uses.\n- **Card attachments (issue #1979)**: a card may carry up to eight files and images. The create and edit forms accept them three ways — drag and drop, paste, and the file picker — and a picked file stays a LOCAL preview until the card is saved: the upload happens on save, so a card the user abandons leaves no stored object behind. The drop area is focusable and keyboard-operable, and the removal controls are disabled while a save is in flight. An image is stored as a raster image and travels with the execution as an image part of the prompt, placed after the text part; any other file is stored verbatim and reaches the execution session as a readable host path in a read-only attachment section of its own, separate from the handover references. The card keeps METADATA only — the kind, the stored identifier, the name, the size, the media type, the digest of the exact stored bytes, and the pixel size of an image — never the bytes, never base64, never a data URL. The display name is always one canonical line without any path part, so it can neither break the prompt nor point at a directory. Before the ledger commits an attachment, the Host proves the claim against the official attachment storage: an image is read back and compared, a file is streamed and its digest recomputed, and a reference the storage cannot prove refuses the whole action, so a spoofed client claim never becomes a stored fact. Every execution resolves the attachments afresh, and a route that declares it cannot read images refuses the run before the prompt is queued. The board's limits are eight attachments per card, 10 MiB per attachment and 32 MiB per card; a deployment whose own attachment storage is stricter — including its per-message image budget — lowers the published limit, and the Host enforces that budget both when it writes the card and when the execution resolves it. One stored object is claimed once: the same content never appears twice on a card.\n- **Host-authoritative ledger**: tasks, schedules, and execution records live in `$DSH_HOME/task-board/ledger-v2.json`; browser actions become confirmed Host transactions.\n- **Bounded execution history**: each task keeps the most recent 20 execution records; the oldest runs are trimmed when a new run starts, so ledger size and write cost stay bounded regardless of how often a task has run.\n- **Real execution**: manual and scheduled runs use the same Host runner, which by default creates a fresh session, renames it, applies the agent preset and `/permission <id>`, then queues the task prompt.\n- **Goal-driven runs (opt-in per card, on top of the global switch)**: the GLOBAL native `/goal` switch (below, off by default) is the master control; with it on, and only when a card opts in through its detail-view checkbox (the new-task dialog starts unchecked), the runner queues the task prompt and then arms dsh's built-in `/goal` with that same composed prompt as the objective. dsh's goal-round driver keeps starting continuation rounds in the session until the agent marks the goal complete, and the board keeps the execution in `running` until the goal leaves its active phase: a completed goal settles the run as succeeded, a blocked one fails it with the goal's own reason. The option is per task (`goalRun`, absent means off, so a card that never touched it runs one plain turn) and is available to `task_board_create`/`task_board_update` too. The checkbox is always operable: the master switch decides whether the preference takes effect, never whether it can be stated, and it never rewrites the stored value.\n- **Goal acceptance (on by default)**: a task executed in goal form must pass ONE acceptance before `update_goal(action: complete)` may take effect, because the board gates that call on the official tool pre-execute lifecycle instead of trusting the agent's own report. Acceptance runs the default final acceptance of the installed `dsh-llm-verifier` (MIT): the three coding criteria (Specification Adherence, Output Match, Error Signal Detection), a 0.65 threshold applied to the total AND to every criterion, two judge rounds per criterion with the A/B slots swapped and averaged, the task's real trajectory (tool calls, their output, assistant prose) judged against the empty-work baseline, the work must beat that baseline, and — when the deployment records workspace changes — the HOST's own record of what the run changed on disk (file list with added/deleted counts and bounded per-file comparisons) is attached as the prompt's reference context so a described-but-unapplied patch cannot pass. A veto is booked as a quality verdict only when it can be LOCATED: every criterion that makes the run fail must arrive with a structured finding naming the requirement it imposes, the observation that falls short, the difference, and a verbatim citation of the task, the work's own trajectory or the host's workspace record. A rejecting answer with no finding, a generic or empty finding, a citation that does not occur in the reviewed evidence, a citation of the empty-work baseline, and a criterion failed without its own evidence are recorded as an INVALID acceptance instead: they spend no quality budget, do not fail the card, and are bounded separately (two), after which the board stops calling the judge and holds the card for a human. A run whose only records are invalid ends for lack of a matching pass, but with its own terminal reason that states the acceptance was unusable and explicitly denies being an evidence-backed quality veto. A judge that could not see the output because the trace was truncated is treated the same way, because insufficient evidence is not a failure of the work. One execution may accept twice: the first failure returns the total, the per-criterion scores and the located findings to the fixing agent, the second failure ends that execution as failed. Once an execution PASSES and settles, the acceptance-only detail (its findings and structured citations) is removed automatically and only a lightweight audit credential remains — verdict, scores, time, judge route, evidence hash and a one-line problem summary. Nothing outside that execution's own acceptance record is touched, a failed or invalid execution keeps everything a repair or a review needs, the removal is idempotent, and a cleanup that fails is recorded and retried on the next Host start without ever revoking the pass. The budget lives on the execution record, so a repeated completion call, a new goal round, a plugin reload and a Host restart all reuse the same cycle, while a rerun or a scheduled occurrence is a new execution with its own budget. An anomaly (timeout, authentication failure, unparseable judge answer, unresolvable judge route) is recorded separately from a quality verdict and never consumes the quality budget. Exhausting the anomaly budget does NOT fail the card: a judge route that cannot answer is the environment failing, not the work, so the cycle is held open with no further judge call until a user clears the recorded anomalies through `task_board_manage(action: reset-verification)`. An attempt that the acceptance time budget ends before any verdict is recorded as its own stage, spends no budget at all and also fails nothing. Both ceilings are settings (`goalVerificationCallTimeoutSeconds`, `goalVerificationBudgetSeconds`), read live, and a judge call is never opened when the time left cannot hold it. The running column shows executing / verifying / fixing, and each execution's row carries its verdict, judge model and level, count, scores with thresholds, findings, evidence scope and token usage. Forced acceptance also keeps the old fallback paths honest: a paused goal, an unreadable projection, a completed turn and a manual settle can no longer settle a goal execution as succeeded without a matching pass record. A failure carrying acceptance records means the judge answered and the work did not pass, while a failure with no acceptance record at all is reported as its own reason: the gate never opened because the session never called `update_goal(action: complete)` — often a session that narrated completion in prose — so nothing was ever judged and the delivery was never rejected. **A single card can opt out of the gate**: the new-task form and the task detail both carry a Skip acceptance checkbox (off by default, a card-level option like Continue in the same conversation and Start with /goal), and a checked card no longer intercepts its completion claim in goal form. The execution records `applicability: skipped` and the report says the CARD skipped acceptance, which is a different fact from the board-wide switch being off and is reported as such. It applies only to executions started afterwards, so flipping it mid-run never rewrites the rule judging a run already in flight.\n- **Task reasoning effort**: the task model picker exposes a reasoning-effort selector when the selected model declares supported levels in the Host model catalog. Leaving it blank inherits the model/Host default; only that model's declared levels are offered. The task stores its choice and applies it when selecting the execution model, including a reused session. This setting is separate from the acceptance judge's reasoning effort.\n- **Optional session reuse**: a task can opt into continuing in its previous execution's session (issue #1419). Reuse happens only when that session is idle and still present in the runtime roster — the Host then re-applies the pinned permission and model on it and queues the prompt, keeping the conversation title and history; otherwise the run mints a fresh session as before, so an unknown roster or a busy session never blocks a scheduled run. The roster read is taken for the launch itself, so a board that has been idle reuses a session that has been idle all along instead of refusing it.\n- **Idle-aware session polling (issue #1821)**: the Host reads the DSH session roster only while the board has something that roster can decide — an execution to inspect, or a card parked in the running column whose verdict may arrive from a settle this process never saw. An empty board with no running card, no open execution and no enabled schedule polls nothing at all, so an idle Host no longer rebuilds every persisted session row (string conversion, object allocation, one stat per record) on a fixed heartbeat. The cadence that governs a busy board is the `sessionPollSeconds` setting, and a roster read that fails or stays unknown backs off on a doubling delay up to one minute, so a session tree that is down is not hammered at the poll interval.\n- **Fail-closed pins**: a missing workspace, missing or broken preset, or rejected permission command fails before the task prompt is sent.\n- **Host scheduler**: 5-field cron supports `*`, `*/n`, ranges, comma lists, and Sunday `0/7`. Each rule carries its own IANA time zone (the Host's zone by default), and day-of-month/day-of-week follow Vixie semantics: both fields restricted means OR, any other combination means AND. Wall-clock gaps at a daylight-saving transition are skipped, and an ambiguous repeated time fires once, at the earlier instant. A rule is either a recurring cron rule — optionally capped by a run limit (unlimited, 1, 2, or any positive whole number) — or a one-shot pinned to a single future instant; the Host counts the executions it actually opens, and a rule that reaches its cap or fires its one-shot stops itself in the ledger rather than waiting for the executed work to disarm it.\n- **Deterministic recovery**: a running execution with a recorded session is observed after restart; an interrupted start without a session id is cancelled and is not resent.\n- **Live synchronization**: mutations return a full revisioned snapshot; SSE announces revision, scheduler, and power changes. The mirror has five re-read entry points: change frames (revision advancing), connection establishment or re-establishment (`EventSource.onopen`), page visibility recovery, stream errors (`EventSource.onerror`, throttled by `STREAM_ERROR_NOTIFY_MS`), and a bounded verification read while the mirror still has unsettled executions (`src/client/pending-verify.ts`, `PENDING_VERIFICATION_MS` 15 seconds, stopped as soon as the last execution settles). A connection can stay open yet stop delivering, in which case there is neither an `onerror` nor a frame, so frames cannot be verified from the browser side. An idle board with no unsettled executions performs zero reads.\n- **Optional idle-sleep protection**: off by default; when enabled it covers every running DSH session, enabled non-archived task-board schedules, and unknown session state.\n- **System-prompt injection**: the Host registers a `plugin:task-board` section (order 200) through `SystemPrompt.section`, and the task-board settings can disable the announcement without disabling the board. The guidance also reminds agents to close any visible `todo_write` plan before the final answer.\n- **Agent tools**: every session gets eight model-facing tools (`task_board_list`, `task_board_get`, `task_board_create`, `task_board_update`, `task_board_set_parent`, `task_board_run`, `task_board_manage`, `task_board_schedule`) that drive the same Host ledger the browser drives, so an agent can list the board, create subtasks, link or detach them, start a run, move a card to any column (declaring it done, failed, or in progress without a run), archive/restore/delete it, settle a card the board can no longer observe, and arm its cron schedule from the conversation.\n- **External outcomes (issue #1826)**: work that is not executed by this Host — an agent outside DSH such as Codex or Claude Code, running its own model — can be recorded as a real run rather than a bare column edit. `task_board_manage(action: 'record-external-outcome', result: 'succeeded'|'failed', initiatedBy: <who>)` appends an execution record carrying the verdict, the caller and an optional summary, and the terminal column is derived from that same record by the same rule a Host settlement uses (`core/tasks.ts` `settledStatus`). The record is marked `external`, never carries a session, and is refused while the card still has an open execution (while this Host is running the card it stays the only authority) and on an archived card. `running` and `cancelled` cannot be recorded this way: those stay Host-only. A manual `move-done`/`move-failed` remains available and still writes only the column — the difference is that this one leaves a record behind, so the column and the run history can never disagree.\n\n- **External provider extensions**: the GitHub Issues extension (`@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-task-board-github`, enabled by default) synchronizes GitHub Issues into board cards. It is a provider of THIS board, so its configuration renders inside this plugin's own settings card — the section only appears while the extension is installed, and its repository/credential form only while the extension is on; see [its README](../dsh-task-board-github/README.md).\n\n## Architecture and protocol\n\nThe board view renders on first open and keeps its local view state when closed and reopened. Host synchronization, scheduling and execution remain active independently of the view.\n\n- `src/index.ts` mounts the Host service through the official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-gateway`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver` SDKs.\n- `src/host-ledger.ts` serializes actions and persists `{ schemaVersion: 6, revision, tasks, scheduler, recentRequests }` through a temporary file plus atomic rename.\n- `src/host-service.ts` owns schedule firing (a single timer armed at the ledger's nearest target through the host's `timer` service, falling back to process timers when the host serves none), missed-trigger skipping, runner launch, restart reconciliation, and power reasons; the ledger itself owns the run budget, so a one-shot or an exhausted capped rule can never be opened a second time.\n- `src/client/native-panel.tsx` registers the board's sidebar row and center-column page (the official `sidebar.panellist` list seat and the keyed `main` seat) and maintains the center-column exclusivity protocol with the ssh panel.\n- `src/client/host-api.ts` imports legacy browser data once, submits idempotent actions, and treats Host snapshots as the only confirmed UI state.\n- Same-origin endpoints are `GET /api/task-board/state`, `GET /api/task-board/events`, and `POST /api/task-board/action`.\n- Every endpoint requires browser authentication. Under the board's own fence that means a browser same-origin marker: `sec-fetch-site: same-origin`, an `Origin` header, or the Host's `dsh-auth-*` browser-auth cookie. The last one is how the DSH Desktop shell reaches the board: it serves the Web GUI from `dsh-app://app/` and forwards that page's requests itself, dropping `Origin` and `sec-fetch-site` and attaching the authority-bound cookie it redeemed from the Host's launch URL at startup. Direct access is restricted to the DSH loopback origin. A deployment DSH itself serves through a trusted reverse proxy or ingress is instead admitted by the Host's `connection` service, which applies its own Host/Origin fence and verifies the signed browser session before the board sees the request; an authenticated same-host proxy that DSH does not front must use an explicit Host allowlist and a server-injected token, and a deployment whose own tunnel dials the loopback upstream can instead turn on `trustForwardedProxy` (see Configuration), which admits that shape on the same-origin marker alone. POST requests additionally require JSON. Ordinary actions are limited to 64 KiB and import to 2 MiB. The action union has no command, executable path, shell text, or arbitrary argument field.\n\n## Agent tools\n\nThe board is operable from a conversation, not only from the GUI. Each tool drives the same Host ledger, so a card created in the GUI is immediately visible to agents and vice versa, and every gate the UI honors still holds. The surface follows the `enabled` switch: a disabled board answers no tool call, and a deployment whose runtime serves no tool registry still mounts the board with the GUI intact.\n\n- `task_board_list` lists cards with filters (column, parent, roots only, label, free-text query, archived) plus the board summary: revision, time zone, subtask depth limit, session-default permission, and column counts.\n- `task_board_get` reads one card in full: prompt, labels, parent link, direct subtasks, execution targets, schedule, permission-gate state, and the last ten execution attempts with their session ids, initiator, and outcome.\n- `task_board_create` creates a task or, with `parentId`, a subtask; execution targets left unset inherit the parent, and the deployment subtask-depth limit applies.\n- `task_board_update` edits content, labels, and execution targets; an empty string clears a target and an empty label array clears the labels.\n- `task_board_set_parent` links an existing card under a parent, or detaches it with an empty parent id.\n- `task_board_run` runs a card now (optionally re-running a settled one) and nothing else: the card gets its own session, the Host opens none for its subtasks, and a card with unfinished subtasks is told which of them its session must dispatch; README](packages/dsh-task-board/README.zh.md)）。任务看板不仅仅是一个可视化卡片界面，更是 DeepSeek Harness 官方 Web GUI 与桌面客户端中的**宿主权威后台长程执行与多 Agent 自动化调度引擎**。任务按“待规划、待办、进行中、已完成、已失败”五列进行全生命周期管理，支持项目分区、粘贴文本 AI 解析与卡片多模态附件（每卡最多 8 个图片或文件附件，经官方附件存储 SHA256 核验，执行时图片作为多模态部件入队、文件以只读路径注入），以 Schema v7 事务账本为权威持久化核心，真正实现了长程任务从拆解、父卡自治派发、对抗质检到外部成果闭环的全流程自动化：\n\n- **宿主权威后台驱动与 7x24 小时离线无人值守**：区别于传统仅在前端网页轮询的脆弱看板，所有卡片流转、调度触发与执行监控完全由 DSH 后端 Host 进程作为唯一权威驱动。支持循环 5 字段 Cron 表达式（绑定 IANA 时区与可选 `maxRuns` 次数预算）与单次未来时刻（`once`）两类定时计划；浏览器仅为异步视图，关闭网页标签页、熄灭屏幕或断开网络，后台智能体会话照常并发执行与原子落盘结算。内置跨平台防休眠电源管理（macOS `caffeinate`、Windows `ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED`、带有 systemd-logind 的 Linux `systemd-inhibit`），允许显示器正常关闭的同时阻止整机因闲置休眠，确保夜间无人值守巡检与流水线准时打卡。\n- **树状子任务与父卡自治派发（Subtask Trees & Autonomous Parent Dispatch）**：复杂工程目标可拆解为 1 至 3 层树状子任务（内置环路与深度护栏）。执行任意卡片只为该卡片自身开启**唯一一个**会话，Host 绝不为子任务批量派生独立会话；当执行的卡片存在未完成后代时，Host 自动在本次运行中强制切入 `liangshen`（梁神模式）调度者预设，并在启动 Prompt 中注入未完成子卡清单，由父会话通过 `task_board_get` 逐张读取子卡详情、按依赖顺序通过 `subagent` 自治派发（互不依赖的子任务并发执行），完工前调用 `task_board_manage({ action: 'record-external-outcome' })` 一次性回填各子卡结论（未显式回填的后代由 Host 在父卡终结时幂等兜底结算）。多张独立卡片在同一时刻触发时，由受控准入队列（`runLaunchWidth`，1 至 16，默认 3）治理并发创建会话的宽度。\n- **对抗式双盲质量验收门禁（No False Completion）**：彻底终结 AI 编程中“自述已完成、实则未改动或改崩溃”的虚假交付顽疾。以 goal 形式执行的任务在 Agent 试图调用 `update_goal(complete)` 宣告完工的瞬间被 Host 强制拦截，必须由独立的裁判模型（可自选模型与思考档位）进行真实验收。验收机制沿用严苛的 Coding 质量判据、0.65 绝对通过阈值，每项判据双轮交换 A/B 位置打分消偏，并严格结合会话执行轨迹与宿主工作区真实磁盘文件的 Diff 行级变更审查。首轮未达标精准下发具象结构化问题引导 Agent 自我修复，两次仍不通过才判负，杜绝敷衍糊弄。\n- **GitHub Issues、云端团队协作与手机远端三路扩展**：通过标准外部提供方契约无缝挂载三大官方扩展：[dsh-client-ui-task-board-github](packages/dsh-task-board-github/README.zh.md) 实现任务看板与 GitHub Issues / PR 状态的双向实时同步，远端 Issue 自动入列驱动 Agent 定位修复、运行测试、创建关联 PR 并在合并后自动关单；[dsh-client-ui-task-board-team](packages/dsh-task-board-team/README.zh.md) 将本地 `dsh-agents` 成员绑定至云端 `team-hub`，按租约领取指派 Issue 为本地镜像卡执行，支持决策问题上报、双向评论（`team_comment`）与审阅打回返工；[dsh-task-board-remote](packages/dsh-task-board-remote/README.zh.md) 将看板能力面（`board.v1`）挂载至远程桥扩展缝，让已配对手机直接读写同一份宿主权威账本。\n- **长程目标驱动、会话持久化与冻结交接包（Freeze Handover）**：任务支持武装内置 `/goal` 引擎进行多轮自主续跑；周期性任务可开启会话复用，保留完整上下文记忆；支持通过 `<<<FREEZE` 协议将会话上下文一键冻结为包含“目标/进度/下一步”的结构化快照，并绑定工作区、预设与权限三元组，接手 Agent 瞬间无缝继承前序成果，同时内置提示词注入防御与来源审计。\n- **企业级权限基线、安全确认门与消费熔断保护**：任务可细粒度钉住工作区、Agent 预设、沙箱权限、执行模型与推理思考强度，钉子校验失败即 Fail-Closed；超出安全基线的高权限操作设有「人工确认门（Permission Gate）」，未在 Web 界面显式放行前坚决拒绝执行与调度，杜绝 Agent 越权危害宿主系统；支持配置看板级每日 Token 消费预算上限（`spendBudgetTokens`），防止后台死循环产生意外费用。\n- **面向智能体的双向工具面与外部成果统一**：向大模型完整暴露 8 个原生工具（`task_board_list`、`task_board_get`、`task_board_create`、`task_board_update`、`task_board_set_parent`、`task_board_run`、`task_board_manage`、`task_board_schedule`），赋予对话中的 Agent 自身查看看板、分解子任务、编排流水线与自动化调度的全套能力；同时支持通过 `record-external-outcome` 统一登记在 Claude Code、Codex 等外部工具中完成的工作，让异构开发流统一汇总至一张看板。\n\n| 多列看板与智能体协作 | 后台定时调度与参数配置 |\n| --- | --- |\n| ![DeepSeek Harness 任务看板界面 — AI 智能体多列任务状态流转与并发执行](docs/screenshots/09-task-board.png) | ![DeepSeek 任务详情与后台定时执行设置 — 智能体参数配置、Cron 调度与执行历史](docs/screenshots/10-task-board-detail-cron.png) |\n\n### 梁神模式（LiangShen Mode · 极简 Persona、PTC 运行时与高效调度引擎）\n\n在新建会话输入框左侧通过专属老虎机拨杆切换，或在“设置 > Agent 预设”中选用。梁神模式（`dsh-liangshen`）是专为追求**极致推理效率、超低静态上下文开销与严苛工程执行纪律**而深度重构的杀手级预设与运行时插件。针对主流大模型在长程编程任务中容易出现的系统提示词冗长膨胀、工具 Schema 挤占上下文、思维链无效空转（如“流水账推理”）以及多轮遗忘退化等痛点，梁神模式通过原生极简提示词、程序化代码工具调用（PTC）、MCP 温和分页与关键事实局部就近投射，提供纯粹而强悍的编程作战体验：\n\n- **极简 Persona 与严苛行动导向纪律（Zero Prompt Waste）**：彻底剥离官方 Standard 预设中冗长繁琐的系统级条文，将提示词极致收敛为单行 Persona 与经过实战千锤百炼的高效工程纪律。内置反思熔断（同一假设推演不超过两轮，缺少事实立即闭合思考并调用原生工具探测，杜绝凭空揣测）、行动导向（思考过程仅用于决定下一步具体操作，严禁在思考中预演完整代码）、并发探索（单轮内并发派发多个独立检测或搜索工具）、YAGNI 与 PDCA 循环（单步验证单一假设，不写冗余注水注释）、以及有界收敛纪律（前置检查最多 2-3 轮即刻收敛，迅速转入实际作答或编辑）。大幅降低静态 Token 占用，让模型注意力百分之百倾注于业务与代码本身。\n- **程序化工具调用传输（PTC · Programmatic Tool Calling）**：彻底终结在每次请求中平铺上百个 JSON Schema 工具参数的低效模式。默认将网络线协议（wire）极致收拢为唯一的 `run_code`（运行 TypeScript 脚本），其余所有工具均通过自动生成的强类型 SDK 在独立的沙箱线程中以代码形式调用。无论系统注册了多少复杂工具，静态传输面始终保持极小体积；模型可原生利用 `Promise.all` 编写并发工具调用，并在程序内预先过滤、聚合、提取关键数据，只将精炼结论回传至对话上下文，从根本上解决大文本输出打爆 Token 的问题。对于习惯原生工具面的场景，亦可在插件设置中一键无缝切换为组装好的原生工具清单（Native）。\n- **MCP 工具温和分页与 LRU 动态激活（Gentle Tool Paging）**：针对海量 MCP 工具或第三方插件扩展，出厂默认启用温和分页（默认匹配 `mcp__*`）。外部工具在初始状态下仅以命名空间摘要形式登记在目录消息中，既不占 wire 协议也不进 SDK 声明；当大模型判定需要使用对应工具时，可自主调用 `tool_activate({ namespace })` 按需挂载。内置 LRU 策略（上限 3 个活跃命名空间），自动淘汰最久未用的命名空间，激活状态在会话压缩与恢复后完整重建，兼具海量工具接入能力与极致小巧的静态 Schema 面。\n- **关键事实登记簿与就近状态投射（Fact Register & Working Context）**：长程多轮对话中大模型极易遗忘早期的关键业务约束或踩过的坑。插件向模型提供专属 `fact_register` 工具，可将用户硬性约束、已确认的架构决策或失败路径登记为单行事实（每条不超过 160 字符，最多保留 12 条）。关键事实随 `[Working Context: ...]` 状态行在每一轮交互中就近投射至最新消息尾部的局部注意力窗口内，从物理机制上彻底解决长上下文“中间遗忘”与重复踩坑顽疾。\n- **原生调度者架构与敏捷访谈纪律（Dispatcher Identity & Triage）**：预设出厂深度集成调度者（Dispatcher）架构规范，赋能模型以团队指挥官身份统领工程任务。内置复杂度分诊机制（L0/L1 单点任务直接敏捷执行，L2 复杂任务严格遵循“澄清访谈 -> 架构规划 -> 并发子代理派发 -> 双层严格验收”标准流）；设定严格的提问预算控制（单轮最多 4 问、总计最多 3 轮、影响面排序、假设先行），杜绝无效拉扯；任务状态权威沉淀于 `todo_write`，杜绝浮躁的敷衍式交付。\n- **新建会话老虎机拨杆与炫酷中奖特效（Composer Slot Lever）**：在新建会话输入框工具行、模型选择器左侧，精心打造了一台复古老虎机拨杆控件。下拉拨杆（支持鼠标拖拽、单击或键盘快捷操作）即可一键为当前新建会话装配梁神模式，拉下命中即触发绚丽的中奖粒子特效（闪光、冲击环、火花粒子与专属彩蛋横幅）；上推即可平滑切回默认模式。拨杆自适应全局主题色彩，且在会话开始后自动隐藏，丝滑灵动，极具极客趣味。\n\n详细机制、评测数据与高级配置参数见 [dsh-liangshen README](packages/dsh-liangshen/README.zh.md)。\n\n### 智能体小队（Agent Squads · 可复用成员定义与整队协同运行）\n\n通过侧边栏“智能体”入口进入。智能体小队（`dsh-agents`）把跨会话复用的专业 AI 角色与团队编制沉淀为宿主权威账本：每个小队管理一组有序成员，既可按需单独点播某个成员开启专属会话，也可一键发起整队 Agent Teams 协同攻坚：\n\n- **可复用小队与成员定义（Reusable Squad & Member Definitions）**：小队支持配置名称、职责描述、可选绑定工作区与整队运行的 Lead 预设；每位成员独立钉住显示名称、Agent 预设（如梁神模式或研究小队预设）、沙箱权限、模型路由、推理思考强度与成员简报（Brief）。成员简报仅通过系统提示词段注入该成员专属会话，绝不污染首条用户消息或普通对话会话。\n- **整队 Agent Teams 协同运行与实时投影（Whole-Squad Runs & Live Projection）**：一键启动整队运行，小队名册与任务目标经 `team:squad` 系统提示词上下文直达 `<小队名> / Lead` 会话；Lead 按成员钉住的预设、权限与模型动态孵化专属 Teammate，任一钉子无法兑现立即 Fail-Closed 报错而不静默降级。前端直接读取共享会话存储中的 `agentTeam` 投影（`stateVersion` 4），实时呈现 Lead 与各 Teammate 的角色、执行阶段与启动异常，全程无需轮询。\n- **10 项全会话定义管理与启动工具（10 Model-Facing Management & Launch Tools）**：向宿主全体会话注册 `squads_list`、`squads_read`、`squads_create`、`squads_update`、`squads_delete`、`squad_member_add`、`squad_member_update`、`squad_member_remove`、`squads_run_member`、`squads_run_squad` 共 10 项进程内工具，支持对话中的 Agent 自主编排小队、点播单成员会话或发起整队运行，删除操作强制要求 `confirm: true` 安全确认。\n- **原子账本持久化与同源运行时避让（Atomic Ledger & Runtime Coexistence）**：定义与最新 200 条运行记录经临时文件 fsync + 原子 rename 持久化于 `$DSH_HOME/dsh-agents/ledger.json`（由 `ledger.json.lock` 保证单进程独占，损坏账本原样保留绝不覆盖）；当宿主已挂载官方 `agentTeams` 服务时自动避让内置团队运行时并无缝复用官方状态投影。\n\n详细契约、工具表与安全模型见 [dsh-agents README](packages/dsh-agents/README.zh.md)。\n\n### 实时浏览器视图（Browser View · 右侧栏 CDP 实时投屏与网页自动化）\n\n在会话右侧栏标签条或引导胶囊中打开。实时浏览器视图（`dsh-browser-view`）为 Agent 提供一个由宿主驱动、用户可在聊天旁侧实时观看的受控 Chromium 浏览器标签页，实现前端开发验证、视觉巡检与网页交互的全程可视化闭环：\n\n- **右侧栏 CDP 实时投屏与保活挂载（Right-Docked Screencast & Keep-Mounted View）**：注册专属右侧栏标签页类型 `browser-view`（与官方 `browser` 标签页和平共处），通过单条 WebSocket 实时绘制 CDP `Page.startScreencast` 画面帧、当前 URL、标题与 Agent 最近一次操作摘要；切换标签 chip 时保持挂载不断连，仅在页面变化时推流。\n- **默认隔离 Chromium 与真实已登录浏览器接管（Isolated Chromium & Real Browser Attach）**：默认惰性拉起带有一次性临时配置目录与随机调试端口的无头 Chromium（固定 1280x800 视口，访问本机 DSH Web GUI 遇 401 鉴权时自动内存取票完成登录）；开启 `realBrowserEnabled` 后可通过本地回环 CDP 端点（默认 `http://127.0.0.1:9222`）直接接管用户以非默认数据目录启动的 Chrome 或 Edge，直接在既有登录态下操作全部标签页，绝不导出或复制任何 Cookie。\n- **11 项受控浏览器交互工具（11 Agent Browser Tools）**：提供 `browser_navigate`、`browser_click`、`browser_type`、`browser_press`、`browser_scroll`、`browser_snapshot`、`browser_screenshot`、`browser_console`、`browser_network`、`browser_tabs`、`browser_close` 完整工具链；`browser_snapshot` 输出深度优先编号（`ref`）与坐标框的 DOM 结构树供精准点击与输入，每个标签页独立维护控制台日志与网络请求环形缓冲区。\n- **高保真无损区域截图与证据入列（Lossless Region Screenshots & Transcript Evidence）**：`browser_screenshot` 默认输出无损 PNG 并经宿主附件服务直接写入对话轨迹；支持传入与 `browser_snapshot` 同坐标系的 `clip: { x, y, width, height }` 进行局部区域裁剪（默认 2x 渲染倍率，可选 1x/2x/3x），显著提升模型视觉 Token 细节分辨率，越界裁剪或连接失败均显式报错而不静默回退。\n\n详细配置、真实浏览器启动参数与安全边界见 [dsh-browser-view README](packages/dsh-browser-view/README.zh.md)。\n\n### 手机 App 远程访问（Mobile Remote · 原生手机 App 接入）\n\n在 profile 中安装 [`@linxin666/dsh-remote-bridge`](packages/dsh-remote-bridge/README.zh.md) 插件并重启服务后，点击侧边栏底部的二维码图标（aria-label 为「配对 iPhone」）打开配对面板。使用手机 App 扫码即可直接开始使用。\n\n配对面板具备本地安全保护，令牌路由（`/remote-bridge/pair/token`）带有回环门控，仅允许在本机浏览器中访问（非本机访问返回 403）。面板生成的配对码为一次性凭据，有效期为 30 秒，点击「重新取码」将作废上一张配对码。二维码编码包含服务地址与令牌的文档（URL 形如 `wss://<origin>/ios/v1?token=...`），手机 App 扫码后即可同时获取服务地址与鉴权令牌。\n\n网络接入协议面仅暴露 `/ios/v1` 一个 WebSocket 端点，隧道与局域网转发均指向仅放行该路径的入站闸门，公网无法直接访问 Web GUI 路由。服务地址按实时状态（中继租约或运行中的隧道）、环境变量 `DSH_REMOTE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` 以及局域网转发器实际监听地址的顺序解析。默认配置下公网可用（中继默认开启、隧道默认关闭、局域网转发默认关闭）；若需在局域网内直连，需在插件配置中开启局域网转发。\n\n[iOS App 还在内测，欢迎来 Discord 交流](https://discord.gg/nBy28kjun)。\n\n### 远程连接（SSH Ops · Web 终端、SFTP 传输与集群运维）\n\n通过侧边栏“SSH”入口打开远程运维面板（详见 [dsh-ssh README](packages/dsh-ssh/README.zh.md)）。支持密钥与密码认证，可一键导入本地 `~/.ssh/config` 主机列表；配置数据安全保存在 `~/.dsh/dsh-ssh.json` 中。面板提供以下操作能力：\n\n- **Web 终端**：基于 xterm.js 的完整远程交互终端，支持实时输出与窗口自适应；\n- **文件传输**：集成 SFTP 上传与下载功能，提供进度提示并支持可视化浏览远程目录；\n- **端口转发**：支持建立本地到远程内部服务的加密隧道（如内网数据库、后端 API），默认仅监听 127.0.0.1 安全地址；\n- **集群并发执行**：支持多主机批量命令执行，并可通过别名、运行环境或标签进行过滤；\n- **Agent 直连调用**：智能体与面板共享主机配置，在会话中发出指令即可委派 Agent 执行远程巡检与运维命令。\n\n### 使用统计（Usage Statistics · Token 消耗追踪、余额预警与 Token 银行）\n\n在“设置 > 使用统计”中集中查看 token 消耗数据、供应商余额以及编程套餐额度，支持自动定时刷新与手动即时查询。\n\n- **用量明细**：查看每日输入、输出与缓存用量，按不同供应商与模型细分展示，并提供最近 30 天消费趋势；支持的供应商提供账户余额查询，针对 DeepSeek 官方路由还提供峰谷分时计费与账单估算。\n- **个人套餐追踪**：实时展示 Kimi、GLM、MiniMax、OpenCode Go、Codex / ChatGPT 等平台编程套餐的使用比例与重置周期。\n- **Token 银行**：所有 provider 每消耗 100 万 tokens 铸造 1 鲸元，以“鲸元券”形式展示台账周期内的累计 token 与调用指标，支持保存票券卡片与系统级分享。\n- **桌面宠物联动**：安装宠物插件后，可通过桌面悬浮挂件的气泡提示直接查看当前会话供应商的额度、余额或今日消耗。\n\n统计自插件首次启用起计，不回填历史数据；鲸元券统计台账窗口内所有 provider 的 tokens（消费行仍只来自 DeepSeek 官方余额观测）。支持的供应商列表与配置细节见 [dsh-usage README](packages/dsh-usage/README.zh.md)。\n\n![DeepSeek Token 用量统计与 Token 银行 — API 消耗追踪与账单估算](docs/screenshots/35-usage-token-bank.webp)\n\n### 会话归档管理（Session Archive Manager · 全文检索与生命周期策略）\n\n会话归档管理（`dsh-session-archive`）是专为解决大量长短期会话堆积而设计的集中管理模块，随全家桶安装生效：\n\n- **集中检索与状态筛选**：统一呈现活跃会话、已归档会话、空白会话、子代理派生会话以及无工作区会话，支持按标题、工作区、状态及会话 ID 进行关键词搜索与多维排序；\n- **安全批量操作**：支持跨筛选结果的多选批量归档、批量恢复以及级联物理删除。执行物理删除时系统将明确提示受影响的后代会话数与预计释放空间，大批量删除需二次确认；当前处于运行中或带有运行中子代理的会话受到严格保护，防止误删；\n- **自动化生命周期策略**：提供两个默认关闭的自动化策略：根据最后活跃时间自动归档、根据归档时间自动清理超期数据，支持在启用前进行结果预览与单次手动执行。\n\n删除操作不可逆，所有管理路由严格限制本机回环访问。详细机制见 [dsh-session-archive README](packages/dsh-session-archive/README.zh.md)。\n\n### 系统要求\n\n- 已安装 DeepSeek Harness 且 `dsh web` 可正常启动。\n- npm 安装方式无需额外环境；若从源码仓库构建，需要 Node.js >= 24.9 与 pnpm 环境。\n\n### 三步上手（npm 安装，推荐）\n\n- **DSH Web CLI（现有浏览器服务）**：\n  1. 先完成三项构建脚本审批（见“安装排障”），再安装聚合包：`dsh plugin --profile web add @linxin666/dsh-web-all@latest`\n  2. 重启 `dsh web` 服务，侧边栏将自动呈现各插件入口\n  3. 打开“设置 > 插件配置”按需开关插件，或在皮肤面板选用主题\n- **官方桌面客户端（DeepSeek Harness Desktop）**：\n  1. 打开官方桌面客户端，进入“设置 → 插件”页面\n  2. 在插件安装框中输入 `@linxin666/dsh-web-all` 并确认安装\n  3. 重启客户端，即可在侧边栏与“设置”中使用各插件功能\n\n> 若仅需要皮肤功能，可单独安装 `@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-skin-center`。若因包管理器门禁安装到旧版本，请参阅后文“安装排障”。\n\n### 从 GitHub 仓库直接安装\n\n仓库根目录声明了标准 `dsh.bundle` 装配清单，支持直接通过仓库地址安装，无需手动克隆代码与构建：\n\n```sh\ndsh plugin --profile web add github:zhu1090093659/dsh-web\n# 或使用完整 git 地址：dsh plugin --profile web add git+https://github.com/zhu1090093659/dsh-web.git\n```\n\n该方式与直接从 npm 安装聚合包效果等价，二者择其一即可。请勿同时通过两种方式安装，以免出现 entry id 冲突。\n\n### 从仓库安装（开发调试）\n\n如需二次开发或调试插件，可按以下步骤从源码构建（要求 Node.js >= 24.9 与 web profile（建议先链接所有子包再注册聚合包）\nnode scripts/link-profile.mjs\ndsh plugin --profile web add link:$(pwd)/packages/dsh-web-all\n\n# 4. 重新启动 dsh web 服务\ndsh web\n```\n\n> 提示：profile 目录未配置为 pnpm 安装排障\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>展开查看常见安装与构建排障方案</strong></summary>\n\n<br>\n\n> **pnpm 严格依赖隔离导致模块找不到**：pnpm 的 isolated 模式默认仅将聚合包放置在顶层，部分子包可能被嵌套收敛，导致 `dsh web` 启动时报错 `Cannot find package '@linxin666/dsh-...'`。若遇到此情况，可在 profile 目录的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 中添加配置 `nodeLinker: hoisted`（或 `public-hoist-pattern: ['@linxin666/*']`）后重新安装。\n\n> **构建脚本被拦截 (ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS)**：这三项审批必须在首次 add 之前就位。正确顺序是重置 profile（官方 `--from-default-profile web`）或换新 profile，在 `<profile>/pnpm-workspace.yaml` 里把三项写成映射，再执行 add：\n>\n> ```yaml\n> allowBuilds:\n>   cloudflared: true\n>   cpu-features: true\n>   ssh2: true\n> ```\n>\n> 必须写成上面的映射形式：列表形式会被 pnpm 改写成 `'0': cloudflared` 之类的占位条目，重跑时还会回退已解析的包（`Packages: -10`）。装失败后补审批重跑会 exit 0，但 `dsh.profile.bundles` 仍无该行：静默半挂载，重跑修不回来，需要先 remove 再 add。已带审批的存量 profile 升级不受影响。\n\n> **pnpm 11 发布时间门禁问题**：在包版本发布后的短时间内，pnpm 11 的默认安全策略（`minimumReleaseAge`）可能会尝试回退拉取旧版本。建议在 profile 目录的 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 中排除相关命名空间以确保获取最新版本：\n>\n> ```yaml\n> minimumReleaseAgeExclude:\n>   - '@linxin666/*'\n> ```\n\n</details>\n\n## 兼容性与运行环境\n\ndsh-web 针对主流操作系统、现代化浏览器及网络拓扑进行了深度工程调优与兼容性保障：\n\n| 维度 | 支持范围与技术规格 |\n| --- | --- |\n| 宿主运行环境 | DeepSeek Harness 常见问题\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>安装重启后，侧边栏未显示插件入口？</strong></summary>\n\n请首先检查插件是否正确安装至 `web` profile（命令需包含 `--profile web`），并通过 `dsh --profile web --dump-config` 验证配置层是否已成功挂载。注意仅刷新网页无法加载新模块，必须彻底重启 `dsh web` 后端服务进程。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>定时任务为何未能按时触发执行？</strong></summary>\n\n任务调度完全由 `dsh web` 后端宿主进程驱动，无需保持前端浏览器页面打开。若宿主进程退出、系统关机或整机进入深度睡眠，错过的触发时间点将遵循跳过策略处理，不执行回填补跑；若任务到达触发点时上一轮仍在运行，会自动顺延至下一个周期。若需要允许息屏但防止主机自动睡眠，可开启任务看板自带的电源保护选项。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>手机 App 配对后为何没有收到流式推送？</strong></summary>\n\n手机 App 通过协议 v1 的 WebSocket 通道与宿主通信。隧道或中继中断期间流式更新暂停，网络恢复后连接会自动重连；更新节奏的差异主要来自广域网往返延迟。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>试穿主题皮肤不满意如何还原？</strong></summary>\n\n皮肤面板提供免落盘试穿功能：点击试穿即刻在当前界面生效预览，离开面板或关闭预览会自动恢复初始外观；只有显式点击“应用”按钮才会将主题配置写入磁盘，可放心预览各类主题。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>是否可以仅使用主题皮肤或某个单一插件？</strong></summary>\n\n完全支持。若仅需要视觉定制，直接安装 `@linxin666/dsh-client-ui-skin-center` 即可；若仅需特定功能，参考“单独安装某个插件”章节直接安装对应 npm 包即可。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>已安装全家桶的前提下，能否额外独立安装某个子插件？</strong></summary>\n\n可以。聚合包内部的插件注册标识均统一带有 `web-ui-` 前缀（例如 `web-ui-usage`），与独立包的原生标识（如 `usage`）相互独立，不会产生 loader entry 重复冲突。宿主服务对同类插件会自动去重。通常情况下安装全家桶即可满足完整需求，无需重复安装单个子包。\n\n</details>\n\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>如何通过手机 App 远程访问 DeepSeek Harness？是否必须在同一 Wi-Fi 下？</strong></summary>\n\n手机远程访问由协议 v1 支撑，不要求必须处于同一 Wi-Fi。默认配置下插件已开启公网中继服务，在电脑端点击侧栏底部的二维码图标打开配对面板后，使用手机 App 扫码即可直接通过公网连接；亦可配置 Cloudflare 隧道。若希望在同一局域网内直连访问，需在插件配置中开启局域网转发并扫码配对。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>关闭浏览器或电脑休眠后，DeepSeek 的定时任务还会继续运行吗？</strong></summary>\n\n任务调度完全由 `dsh web` 后端宿主进程驱动，关闭浏览器标签页不影响定时任务的触发与执行。但如果整机进入深度睡眠或关机，宿主进程将暂停运行，离线期间错过的触发点会遵循跳过策略处理。若希望保持无人值守后台自动化，可在任务看板设置中开启“电源保护”选项，该选项会阻止系统因空闲进入休眠（允许显示器正常熄灭），确保定时任务准时触发。\n\n</details>\n\n<details>\n<summary><strong>如何查看和监控 DeepSeek 及其他模型 API 的 Token 消耗与账户余额？</strong></summary>\n\n安装使用统计插件后，在“设置 > 使用统计”面板中可查看按日汇总的输入、输出与缓存 Token 数量，支持按模型细分查看 30 天消费趋势。针对 DeepSeek 官方路由还提供峰谷分时计费估算；若配置了支持查询余额的供应商 API，插件可定时拉取当前账户剩余额度与重置周期。\n\n</details>\n\n## 已知限制\n\n- 任务看板由后端 Host 进程统一调度，关闭前端标签页不影响任务执行；但若宿主进程停止或操作系统关机睡眠，处于离线期间的触发点将直接跳过不补跑。可选的电源保护仅阻止系统闲置睡眠，无法阻止用户主动合盖、手动休眠或电源切断，技术细节见 [dsh-task-board README](packages/dsh-task-board/README.zh.md)。\n- SSH 凭据（密码与私钥口令）保存在本地 `~/.dsh/dsh-ssh.json` 文件中（文件权限为 0600）；在网络中断重连时可能重新发送非幂等命令，终端输出保持原样返回不执行脱敏，安全规范见 [dsh-ssh README](packages/dsh-ssh/README.zh.md)。\n- 手机 App 流式交互经隧道或中继转发，广域网往返延迟叠加在每次更新上；固定域名中继比裸快速隧道多一跳，两者均可使用。\n- 从源码构建全仓需要 Node.js >= 24.9 与 pnpm 工具链，直接从 npm 安装不受此限制。\n\n##       "path": "packages/dsh-task-board/src/core/handover.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Handover bundle (issue #5, ADR 0001): the resource reference set a\n * continuation card carries — the pinned execution triplet (workspace /\n * agent preset / permission) plus doc/script references — so a picking-up\n * session can start with zero context.\n *\n * Security gate (adversarial scenario b): a bundle whose effective\n * permission is HIGHER than the session default is an unconfirmed binding.\n * It enters the pending-confirmation state (the card stores the binding\n * without a permissionConfirmedAt stamp); manual execution refuses, cron\n * refuses to schedule, and the human confirm-permission action resolves the\n * transaction by stamping the confirmation. Any later permission or\n * handover change re-arms the gate (the confirmation binds the exact\n * permission value, blocking confirm-then-swap escalation).\n */\nimport { isTaskPermission, type TaskPermission, type TaskRecord } from './tasks.ts'\n\nexport type { TaskPermission }\n\n/** Wire shape of a handover bundle (before bundledAt is stamped). */\nexport interface TaskHandoverInput {\n  workspaceId?: string\n  mode?: string\n  permission?: TaskPermission\n  references: string[]\n}\n\n/** Persisted handover bundle on a task record. */\nexport interface TaskHandover extends TaskHandoverInput {\n  /** When the bundle was attached/replaced (ms epoch, stamped by the use case). */\n  bundledAt: number\n}\n\n/** Most references a bundle may carry. */\nexport const HANDOVER_MAX_REFERENCES = 32\n/** Per-reference UTF-8 byte cap. */\nexport const HANDOVER_MAX_REFERENCE_BYTES = 512\n/** Total references UTF-8 byte cap. */\nexport const HANDOVER_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 8 * 1024\n/** Per target-id (workspace/preset) byte cap. */\nexport const HANDOVER_MAX_TARGET_BYTES = 256\n\n/**\n * Fail-safe baseline for the confirmation gate: what it falls back to when the\n * deployment pins no baseline of its own and the Host's default permission\n * preset cannot be read. Every elevation above it stays gated.\n */\nexport const DEFAULT_SESSION_PERMISSION: TaskPermission = 'read-only'\n\n/** Permission elevation rank (higher = more authority). */\nexport const PERMISSION_RANK: ReadonlyMap<TaskPermission, number> = new Map([\n  ['read-only', 0],\n  ['workspace-write', 1],\n  ['danger-full-access', 2],\n])\n\nfunction byteLength(value: string): number {\n  return new TextEncoder().encode(value).length\n}\n\n/**\n * Gate a handover bundle from the wire or disk: exact keys, string targets\n * under the byte cap, a known permission, and a bounded string reference\n * list. Returns the sanitized bundle, or undefined when rejected.\n */\nexport function sanitizeHandover(value: unknown): TaskHandoverInput | undefined {\n  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) return undefined\n  const bundle = value as Record<string, unknown>\n  const keys = Object.keys(bundle)\n  if (!keys.every(key => ['workspaceId', 'mode', 'permission', 'references'].includes(key))) return undefined\n  if (!Array.isArray(bundle.references)) return undefined\n  if (bundle.references.length > HANDOVER_MAX_REFERENCES) return undefined\n  let total = 0\n  for (const reference of bundle.references) {\n    if (typeof reference !== 'string' || reference === '') return undefined\n    const size = byteLength(reference)\n    if (size > HANDOVER_MAX_REFERENCE_BYTES) return undefined\n    total += size\n    if (total > HANDOVER_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES) return undefined\n  }\n  for (const key of ['workspaceId', 'mode'] as const) {\n    const target: unknown = bundle[key]\n    if (target !== undefined && (typeof target !== 'string' || byteLength(target) > HANDOVER_MAX_TARGET_BYTES)) return undefined\n  }\n  if (bundle.permission !== undefined && !isTaskPermission(bundle.permission)) return undefined\n  const workspaceId = bundle.workspaceId\n  const mode = bundle.mode\n  return {\n    ...(typeof workspaceId === 'string' ? { workspaceId } : {}),\n    ...(typeof mode === 'string' ? { mode } : {}),\n    ...(bundle.permission === undefined ? {} : { permission: bundle.permission as TaskPermission }),\n    references: [...bundle.references as string[]],\n  }\n}\n\n/** Build the persisted bundle from a sanitized input, stamping bundledAt. */\nexport function handoverOf(input: TaskHandoverInput, now: number): TaskHandover {\n  return { ...input, bundledAt: now }\n}\n\n/** The permission an execution session would actually run under. */\nexport function effectivePermission(task: Pick<TaskRecord, 'permission' | 'handover'>): TaskPermission | undefined {\n  return task.handover?.permission ?? task.permission\n}\n\n/** Whether a binding's permission is elevated above the session default. */\nexport function exceedsSessionDefault(permission: TaskPermission | undefined, sessionDefault: TaskPermission): boolean {\n  if (permission === undefined) return false\n  return (PERMISSION_RANK.get(permission) ?? -1) > (PERMISSION_RANK.get(sessionDefault) ?? -1)\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether a session running at `holder` already carries `permission`: the\n * permission is absent, or its rank does not exceed the holder's. A teammate\n * inherits the Lead session's permission and cannot be narrowed below it, so a\n * subtask's own pin is carried by a team run exactly when this holds, and a pin\n * it does not carry would be silently dropped instead.\n */\nexport function permissionCarriedBy(holder: TaskPermission, permission: TaskPermission | undefined): boolean {\n  return !exceedsSessionDefault(permission, holder)\n}\n\n/**\n * The confirmation-gate predicate: an elevated permission without a human\n * confirmation stamp. Manual run/rerun and cron must refuse such a card.\n */\nexport function requiresPermissionConfirmation(\n  task: Pick<TaskRecord, 'permission' | 'handover' | 'permissionConfirmedAt'>,\n  sessionDefault: TaskPermission = DEFAULT_SESSION_PERMISSION,\n): boolean {\n  return exceedsSessionDefault(effectivePermission(task), sessionDefault) && task.permissionConfirmedAt === undefined\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "packages/dsh-task-board/src/core/spend-budget.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * The daily token ceiling both spend gates share, as pure rules: the cap\n * comparison and the one refusal wording.\n *\n * The unit is tokens, not money. The usage ledger the board reads prices only\n * DeepSeek's own routes, so a cost cap would read 0 on every other route and\n * refuse nothing on exactly the deployments that need it. A cap of 0 is the\n * shipped default and means \"no gate\": both gates answer before they read a\n * file, subscribe to an event, or compute anything.\n * @module @linxin666/dsh-task-board/core/spend-budget\n */\n\n/** Token cap one board day may spend; 0 disables the gate. */\nexport const DEFAULT_SPEND_BUDGET_TOKENS = 0\n\n/**\n * Whether a day's measured spend already reached the cap.\n * @param usedTokens - tokens the day's spend measurement reported.\n * @param cap - the configured cap, 0 for \"no gate\".\n * @returns true when a run must be refused.\n */\nexport function spendCapReached(usedTokens: number, cap: number): boolean {\n  return cap > 0 && usedTokens >= cap\n}\n\n/**\n * The refusal text both gates report: the thrown message a client sees as\n * board-refused, and the scheduler error a due occurrence records.\n * @param usedTokens - tokens the day's spend measurement reported.\n * @param cap - the configured cap.\n * @returns the refusal message.\n */\nexport function spendCapMessage(usedTokens: number, cap: number): string {\n  return `spend cap reached: ${usedTokens} tokens of ${cap} today; raise the cap in the task board settings`\n}\n"
    },
    {
      "path": "packages/dsh-task-board/src/core/use-cases/task-update.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * Update-task use case: apply an editable-field patch (title/description/\n * prompt plus the execution targets workspaceId/mode/permission) with a\n * fresh updatedAt. Pure ledger transition (no persistence or notify — the\n * controller orchestrates those).\n *\n * An explicit `undefined` in the patch clears the field (the task falls\n * back to the runtime default); an unknown permission string is ignored so\n * stale UI can never persist a value the execution service rejects.\n */\nimport { freezeOf, isTaskPermission, normalizeTags, normalizeTargetId, type TaskRecord, type TaskPermission, type TaskTag } from '../tasks.ts'\nimport { normalizeAttachments, type TaskAttachment } from '../attachment.ts'\nimport type { FreezeSnapshot } from '../freeze-snapshot.ts'\nimport type { TaskHandoverInput } from '../handover.ts'\n\n/**\n * Editable fields on a task (the update patch surface). `freeze` replaces the\n * continuation-card snapshot (restamping frozenAt); an explicit null clears it.\n */\nexport type TaskUpdatePatch = Partial<Pick<TaskRecord, 'title' | 'description' | 'prompt' | 'workspaceId' | 'mode' | 'permission' | 'model' | 'reasoningEffort' | 'reuseSession' | 'goalRun' | 'skipVerification'>> & {\n  freeze?: FreezeSnapshot & { redacted?: boolean } | null\n  /** Replaces the handover bundle (restamping bundledAt); an explicit null clears it. */\n  handover?: TaskHandoverInput | null\n  /**\n   * Replaces the task's labels (issue #1521). Unlike the content fields, tags\n   * stay editable after the first run: they classify the task and shape the\n   * NEXT execution prompt, they are not the record of what already ran. An\n   * explicit null (or a list that normalizes to nothing) clears them.\n   */\n  tags?: TaskTag[] | null\n  /**\n   * Replaces the card's attachments (issue #1979).\n   *\n   * The attachments freeze WITH the card content: they are part of what the\n   * card hands to its execution, so an executed or archived card keeps the\n   * ones it ran with, exactly as it keeps the prompt it ran with. An explicit\n   * null clears them; a present array replaces the whole set.\n   */\n  attachments?: TaskAttachment[] | null\n}\n\n/** The fields that edit the task's content (what the user reads and what the\n * next execution sends). Unlike the execution targets they stay editable only\n * while the task has never started executing — after the first run the\n * recorded prompt is the record of what actually ran, so it becomes read-only.\n */\nexport const TASK_CONTENT_FIELDS = ['title', 'description', 'prompt'] as const\n\n/**\n * The fields that freeze with the card content: the text the card says AND\n * the attachments it carries.\n *\n * The attachments freeze with the content because they ARE part of what the\n * card hands to its execution: a card whose first run already consumed an\n * image keeps that image, and the record of what ran stays what it was. An\n * executed or archived card therefore refuses an attachment change exactly\n * as it refuses a prompt change.\n */\nexport const TASK_FROZEN_FIELDS = [...TASK_CONTENT_FIELDS, 'attachments'] as const\n\n/** Whether an update patch touches any task-content field. */\nexport function hasContentPatch(patch: TaskUpdatePatch): boolean {\n  return (TASK_FROZEN_FIELDS as readonly string[]).some(field => field in patch)\n}\n\n/**\n * Whether a task's content may still be edited: the task must be on-board\n * (not archived) and must never have started executing. Fail-closed: a task\n * with any execution record — running, settled, or cancelled before launch —\n * keeps its content fixed. The run, not the column, is the trigger: a card\n * parked in 'running' by hand has nothing recorded yet and stays editable.\n */\nexport function canEditTaskContent(task: TaskRecord): boolean {\n  return task.archivedAt === undefined && task.executions.length === 0\n}\n\n/** Keep an unknown permission string from entering the ledger. */\nfunction normalizePermission(\n  current: TaskPermission | undefined,\n  value: TaskPermission | undefined,\n): TaskPermission | undefined {\n  if (value === undefined) return undefined\n  return isTaskPermission(value) ? value : current\n}\n\n/**\n * Apply an update across the ledger. Tasks that do not match the id are left\n * untouched; the matched task receives the patch plus a fresh updatedAt.\n * @param tasks - current ledger.\n * @param id - the task to update.\n * @param patch - editable-field changes.\n * @param now - clock instant (ms epoch).\n */\nexport function applyUpdateTask(\n  tasks: readonly TaskRecord[],\n  id: string,\n  patch: TaskUpdatePatch,\n  now: number,\n): readonly TaskRecord[] {\n  return tasks.map(task => {\n    if (task.id !== id) return task\n    const { freeze: freezePatch, handover: handoverPatch, tags: tagsPatch, attachments: attachmentsPatch, ...rest } = patch\n    const workspaceId = 'workspaceId' in patch ? normalizeTargetId(patch.workspaceId) : undefined\n    const mode = 'mode' in patch ? normalizeTargetId(patch.mode) : undefined\n    const permission = 'permission' in patch ? normalizePermission(task.permission, patch.permission) : undefined\n    const model = 'model' in patch ? normalizeTargetId(patch.model) : undefined\n    const reasoningEffort = 'reasoningEffort' in patch ? normalizeTargetId(patch.reasoningEffort) : undefined\n    const next: TaskRecord = { ...task, ...rest, updatedAt: now }\n    // Content fields normalize like creation does (trimmed); an explicit\n    // undefined keeps the current value — content cannot be cleared.\n    for (const field of TASK_CONTENT_FIELDS) {\n      if (!(field in patch)) continue\n      const value = patch[field]\n      next[field] = value === undefined ? task[field] : value.trim()\n    }\n    // null (or a vanished key value) clears the snapshot; a present object\n    // replaces it with a fresh frozenAt stamp.\n    next.freeze = freezePatch == null ? undefined : freezeOf(freezePatch, now)\n    // Handover follows the same null-clears convention, restamping bundledAt.\n    next.handover = handoverPatch == null ? undefined : { ...handoverPatch, bundledAt: now }\n    // Tags use the same convention: a present array replaces the set (after\n    // repair), an explicit null or a fully-invalid list clears it.\n    if ('tags' in patch) next.tags = tagsPatch == null ? undefined : normalizeTags(tagsPatch)\n    // Attachments follow the same convention: a present array replaces the\n    // whole set (after repair), an explicit null clears it.\n    if ('attachments' in patch) next.attachments = attachmentsPatch == null ? undefined : normalizeAttachments(attachmentsPatch)\n    // The permission confirmation binds the exact permission value: a change\n    // of the pinned permission or of the handover bundle re-arms the gate\n    // (blocking confirm-then-swap escalation). handover was destructured out\n    // of rest above, so the stamp survives only when explicitly kept.\n    if (('permission' in patch && patch.permission !== undefined && patch.permission !== task.permission) || 'handover' in patch) {\n      next.permissionConfirmedAt = undefined\n    }\n    // Session reuse is a boolean opt-in; false (or an explicit null from a\n    // caller that needs to clear it) returns the task to one session per run.\n    if ('reuseSession' in patch) next.reuseSession = patch.reuseSession === true ? null : scheduleView(task.schedule),\n          task: taskSummary(task, snapshot.tasks, snapshot.sessionDefaultPermission),\n        })\n      } catch (error) {\n        return refused('refused', messageOf(error))\n      }\n    },\n  })\n}\n\n\nfunction buildListTool(host: TaskBoardToolHost): ToolDefinition {\n  return defineTool({\n    name: 'task_board_list',\n    description: [\n      'List tasks on the DSH task board (the Host-authoritative ledger behind the Web GUI task board).',\n      'Filters: status column, parentId (direct subtasks), rootsOnly, tag, free-text query, and archived inclusion.',\n      'Returns each task id, title, column, parent/subtask link, execution targets, schedule and latest run outcome, plus the board summary (revision, time zone, subtask depth limit, session-default permission).',\n      'Use task_board_get for one task in full, task_board_create to add work, and task_board_run to execute it.',\n    ].join(' '),\n    parameters: {\n      status: { type: 'string', enum: ['backlog', 'todo', 'running', 'done', 'failed'], description: 'Only cards in this column.' },\n      parentId: { type: 'string', description: 'Only the direct subtasks of this task id.' },\n      rootsOnly: { type: 'boolean', description: 'Only tasks that have no parent (default false).' },\n      includeArchived: { type: 'boolean', description: 'Include archived tasks (default false).' },\n      tag: { type: 'string', description: 'Only tasks carrying this label name.' },\n      query: { type: 'string', description: 'Case-insensitive match against title, description, prompt, and label names.' },\n      limit: { type: 'integer', description: 'Maximum rows to return (default 50, maximum 200).' },\n    },\n    output: { schema: { type: 'json' }, render: renderJson },\n    isConcurrencySafe: () => true,\n    async execute(args) {\n      const snapshot = host.snapshot()\n      const needle = typeof args.query === 'string' ? args.query.trim().toLowerCase() : ''\n      const limit = Math.min(Math.max(typeof args.limit === 'number' ? Math.trunc(args.limit) : 50, 1), 200)\n      const matched = snapshot.tasks.filter(task => {\n        if (args.includeArchived !== true && task.archivedAt !== undefined) return false\n        if (args.status !== undefined && task.status !== args.status) return false\n        if (args.parentId !== undefined && task.parentId !== args.parentId) return false\n        if (args.rootsOnly === true && task.parentId !== undefined) return false\n        if (args.tag !== undefined && !(task.tags ?? Use mode \"once\" with at for a single future run, or mode \"cron\" (or omit mode) with a 5-field cron expression, optionally capped by maxRuns.',\n        properties: {\n          enabled: { type: 'boolean', required: true, description: 'Whether the schedule is armed.' },\n          mode: { type: 'string', enum: ['cron', 'once'], description: 'The kind of plan: \"cron\" for a recurring rule, \"once\" for a single future instant.' },\n          cron: { type: 'string', description: '5-field cron of a recurring rule: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week.' },\n          at: { type: 'integer', description: 'Planned instant of a one-shot, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC). undefined : args.permission\n      }\n      if (has(args, 'reuseSession')) patch.reuseSession = args.reuseSession === true\n      if (has(args, 'goalRun')) patch.goalRun = args.goalRun === true ? true : false\n      if (has(args, 'skipVerification')) patch.skipVerification = args.skipVerification === true ?       "path": "packages/dsh-task-board/src/host/llm-dispatch.ts",
      "content": "/**\n * One-shot model dispatch for the board's Host half.\n *\n * The board makes two one-shot model calls: the goal-acceptance judge\n * (`verification-runner.ts`) and the \"parse pasted text\" action\n * (`host-ai.ts`). Both call the official `llm` service, and both must call it\n * the way the official agent loop does.\n *\n * The runtime exposes two entry points with the same name shape. The public\n * `stream(options)` is a single-argument convenience method, and it is an\n * ordinary instance property — any plugin may overwrite it. The registration\n * bound path `prepareCall(config)` returns a one-shot handle whose\n * `stream(request)` reaches the adapter through the runtime's internal\n * dispatch instead, and `ctx.on('llm/stream')` remains the supported seam every\n * extension is expected to register on.\n *\n * A third-party provider plugin that patched `llm.stream` with the waterfall\n * listener signature `(options, next)` broke every caller that used the public\n * method: `llm.stream(options)` invoked the listener with `next === undefined`,\n * so the guard's `for await (const chunk of next())` raised\n * `TypeError: next(...) is not a function or its return value is not async\n * iterable`. The agent loop was unaffected because it already dispatches\n * through `prepareCall(...).stream(...)`; the board's two one-shot calls were\n * not, and each completed acceptance was recorded as an anomaly\n * (\"验收异常（裁判请求失败）\") after two judge attempts.\n *\n * Dispatching through the prepared call fixes that at the owner: the board no\n * longer depends on a mutable instance property that a plugin may legitimately\n * replace, and a plugin that registers on `llm/stream` is still invoked. The\n * public method remains the fallback for a runtime that exposes no\n * `prepareCall` at all, so an older or proxied service keeps working.\n */\nimport { ReasoningEffortId, type GenerateOptions, type LlmCallConfig, type LlmRuntime, type StreamChunk } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm'\n\n/** The request fields the board adds around a call config. */\nexport type OneShotRequest = Pick<GenerateOptions, 'messages' | 'signal'> & Pick<GenerateOptions, 'system'>\n\n/**\n * The call config as this board's own domain types carry it.\n *\n * `VerificationRoute.reasoningEffort` and the parse route are plain strings (the\n * catalog publishes effort ids as strings), while the SDK brands them\n * nominally; the single crossing is branded here so no caller repeats the\n * assertion.\n */\nexport interface OneShotCallConfig {\n  provider: string\n  model: string\n  reasoningEffort?: string\n  temperature?: number\n  maxTokens?: number\n}\n\n/** The runtime shape this dispatch looks for beyond the public interface. */\ntype PreparedRuntime = LlmRuntime & { prepareCall?: LlmRuntime['prepareCall'] }\n\n/**\n * Open one one-shot model stream on the registration-bound dispatch path.\n *\n * The call-config fields must travel inside `config` (not the request): the\n * prepared handle refuses a request whose config fields differ from the ones it\n * resolved, so the request carries only messages, signal, and the optional\n * one-shot system prompt.\n * @param llm - the Host's llm service.\n * @param config - provider/model route plus the caller's sampling controls.\n * @param request - the assembled messages and cancellation for this call.\n * @returns the chunk stream, including any registered `llm/stream` listener.\n */\nexport async function openOneShotStream(\n  llm: LlmRuntime,\n  config: OneShotCallConfig,\n  request: OneShotRequest,\n): Promise<AsyncIterable<StreamChunk>> {\n  const call: LlmCallConfig = {\n    provider: config.provider,\n    model: config.model,\n    ...(config.reasoningEffort === undefined ? {} : { reasoningEffort: ReasoningEffortId(config.reasoningEffort) }),\n    ...(config.temperature === undefined ? {} : { temperature: config.temperature }),\n    ...(config.maxTokens === undefined ? {} : { maxTokens: config.maxTokens }),\n  }\n  const runtime = llm as PreparedRuntime\n  if (typeof runtime.prepareCall !== 'function') {\n    return llm.stream({ ...call, ...request } as GenerateOptions)\n  }\n  const prepared = await runtime.prepareCall(call, request.signal)\n  return prepared.stream({ ...prepared.config, ...request })\n}\n"
    },
